drainage.summary: Built in a former sand-and-gravel quarry with sandy soil, it is regularly named one of Western Washington's best-draining winter courses. Reviewers say it plays softer and slower in winter but rarely becomes unplayable.
Sandy soil and fescue turf in arid Eastern Washington. It rarely gets rain, but when it does the sand drains very well and the course plays firm and fast.

Reviewers report soaked, soggy fairways after rain and say the fairways don't drain especially well. Some add that it held up acceptably after record rain and has improved under a new superintendent.

Built on sandy, dune-like high-desert ground above the Columbia River with fine fescue that plays firm and fast; rain is rare in Brewster, and when it comes the sand drains it right away.
Cascade Golfer names it one of the winter courses built on a bed of sand, which drains far better than courses built on dirt. It also sits in Sequim's rain shadow, so it gets less rain to begin with.

Reports are mixed. One reviewer found it very playable after four days of heavy rain, but others describe soggy fairways and cart-path-only days in fall, and wet fairways are called normal for the season.

Reports are mixed. One golfer found plugged balls on very wet fairways in August and blamed overwatering, another found the ground hard and dry, and reviewers mention drainage work under way on hole 18.

drainage.summary: This is a dry-climate course: the back nine is cut through desert terrain above the Columbia and rain is rare. We found no golfer reports about how it handles rain; one reviewer mentioned patchy, dry areas.
This is a dry-climate Tri-Cities course. Reviewers say firm, fast greens are the norm there and describe the bunkers as firm rather than muddy. We found no complaints about wet conditions.

This course is on the drier east side of the Cascades. A reviewer described very firm greens and good fairway roll, with sun and wind drying the course out during the day. We found no reports of wet conditions.
